newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European airports increase retail revenue, traffic.
newsitem.headline: European airports increase retail revenue, traffic.

text.p: European airports have lowered charges to airlines during the last decade while raising commercial and retail revenue and handling more passengers, an Airports Council International study said on Wednesday.
Council remarks stemmed from its report on trends over the period of 1988 to 1995 involving 51 airports, in seven EU countries, between them accounting for 55 percent of European air traffic.
Over that time, commercial revenues at the sample airports grew 15 percent, while passenger and cargo volumes grew 40 percent," ACI said in a statement.

"To cope with constant traffic growth, Europe's airports increased their annual investments by between five percent and six percent, while leaving charges to their airline customers untouched," ACI Europe Director General Philippe Hamon said.

ACI Europe represents the interests of 341 airports in the 48 countries of its European region, handling 90 percent of commercial air traffic, 730 million passengers and more than 10 million tonnes of cargo.
